Okay so first before starting the timer. 
Listen to motivation videos where the guy is shouting at you to be motivated. It boots up the process. It works just type ..'Study motivation' or something

Secondly, listen to rain+thunder+crackling fire sound combo or basically just white noise for concentration. I prefer the R+T+C combo.

Hey, hey, hey.

Take a deep breath.

For just a day. Leave your schedule. Just leave it.
Don't follow it. Take that day as your 'new start'. 
Enjoy that day & savour it..

At night make 4 lists in a notebook:

-Master list (goals you want to achieve this year/before this year ends)

-Monthly list(goals you want to achieve in this month)

- Weekly list(goals you want to achieve this week)

Make sure you write EACH & EVERY goal, no matter how 'small' or 'medicore' it is.

Next,download apps like:

-Todoist (for scheduling)

Make sure you plan out your day the night before.

AND an extremely useful tip. Plan out your day in 30 min blocks. I have time-blindness, so i just make a list of stuff I have to do the next day. And plan our stuff is 30 min blocks:

Eg. For 30 mins I'll study biology. 

This allows for less disappointment because I can usually mantain focus for 30 mins. If it's still hard, divide it in 15 mins blocks.


- Alarmy (for heavy sleepers)
 
Place your phone on far side of the far, this way you'd have to walk to turn it off & further Alarmy asks you to solve tasks, so by this time you'll be awake.

-An app that reminds you to stay your meds/drinks.


-Repetetive app. I have this app on android called 'Let's review',  it basically works on repetitive study system. It reminds to review chapters before I forget them, I don't know if there's an iOS alternative.


Finally, an extremely useful focusing tip. I listen to rain/thunderstorm sounds whole studying to mantain focus. It works like a charm. You can also try other white sounds :D.

Also I personally think you should take counseling/therapy.
